Great! The apply_template returned a tuple of precursor pairs. The result is a string representation of a tuple of tuples: each inner tuple contains two SMILES strings (precursor1, precursor2). We need to return a list of lists where each inner list contains SMILES strings of each precursor.

We have two possible outcomes:

1. ('C=C(c1ccc([C@H]2C[C@]3(C)C(=O)CC[C@@H]3[C@H]3CCC4=CC5(CCC4=C23)OCCO5)cc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)F', 'CC(=O)c1ccccc1')
2. ('C=C(c1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)F', 'C[C@]12C[C@H](c3ccccc3)C3=C4CCC5(C=C4CC[C@@H]3[C@H]1CCC2=O)OCCO5')

We need to output as list of lists: [["SMILES1","SMILES2"], ["SMILES3","SMILES4"]].

Make sure to preserve exact SMILES strings.

Check for any spaces or quotes. We'll output:

[['C=C(c1ccc([C@H]2C[C@]3(C)C(=O)CC[C@@H]3[C@H]3CCC4=CC5(CCC4=C23)OCCO5)cc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)F','CC(=O)c1ccccc1'], ['C=C(c1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)F','C[C@]12C[C@H](c3ccccc3)C3=C4CCC5(C=C4CC[C@@H]3[C@H]1CCC2=O)OCCO5']]

Return as final answer.
